fields.Summary: A single application opens 60+ LGBTQ+ community scholarship funds for students who are LGBTQ+ or allies and reside in Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington. Montana residents are explicitly eligible and may study anywhere; it covers community college, 4-year, and trade/vocational study. The cycle runs roughly October to January.

Point Foundation's flagship national scholarship supports LGBTQ+ students and allies and is open to applicants who are at least a high-school senior. It is a need-based award renewable for up to four years and requires a 3.3 GPA and a demonstrated connection and commitment to the LGBTQ+ community. The window runs September to late November.

rows.source_name: Fisher House Scholarships for Military Children

fields.Name of Scholarship: Fisher House Scholarships for Military Children
fields.Summary: A $2,000 scholarship for unmarried military dependent children under age 23 with a valid military ID, whose parent is active-duty, Guard/Reserve, retired, or deceased. High-school senior applicants need a 3.0 GPA and full-time enrollment in an accredited 2- or 4-year program.

For children and grandchildren of honorably discharged U.S. veterans or active military, open to 12th graders entering college the fall of their graduation year. Pays $1,000/year (up to $4,000) toward a bachelor's at an accredited 4-year school; requires demonstrated financial need (FAFSA). Window runs January through April 30.

fields.Due Date: Apply via campus — by 3rd week of 1st semester
fields.Application Link/Method: Apply through MUS campus financial aid — mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Waivers
fields.Summary: A last-dollar waiver covering in-state tuition for enlisted members of the Montana Army or Air National Guard in good standing who have completed Initial Entry Training. This is not a family benefit — the student themselves must be a Guard member. Apply through your MUS campus.

fields.Due Date: Apply via campus — by 3rd week of 1st semester
fields.Application Link/Method: Apply through MUS campus financial aid — mus.edu/Prepare/Pay/Waivers
fields.Summary: Waives undergraduate tuition at Montana University System campuses for Montana-resident children (age 25 or under) of service members who were Montana residents at entry to service and were killed in action or died of a service-connected cause. Cannot be combined with other waivers; does not cover fees.

A highly selective last-dollar scholarship for Pell-eligible high-school seniors who are African American, Hispanic American, Native American/Alaska Native, or Asian & Pacific Islander American. Requires a minimum 3.3 weighted GPA and full-time enrollment in a four-year degree. (Active successor to the discontinued Gates Millennium Scholars program.)

Funds undergraduate and graduate study for enrolled Confederated Salish & Kootenai Tribes (CSKT) members who hold a high-school diploma or GED/HiSET and are accepted to an accredited institution. Reapply each year; applications open in January with a May 1 deadline.

A higher-education grant for enrolled members of the Blackfeet Tribe pursuing an undergraduate degree or certificate at an accredited institution; requires certification of Blackfeet blood. Awards are roughly $2,800–$3,000 with a March 1 deadline. (Confirm amount with the Blackfeet Education Department.)

rows.source_name: Louise A. Dean All Montana Tribal Nations Scholarship

fields.Name of Scholarship: Louise A. Dean All Montana Tribal Nations Scholarship
fields.Summary: A need-based scholarship for members of any Montana tribal nation (Assiniboine, Blackfeet, Gros Ventre, Chippewa Cree, Crow, Kootenai, Little Shell, Northern Cheyenne, Pend d'Oreille, Salish, or Sioux) pursuing a certificate, associate, or bachelor's degree. Open to graduating high-school seniors; requires a 2.25 GPA and proof of financial need. Window Jan 1 to Mar 31.

Covers undergraduate tuition at Montana University System campuses for enrolled members or tribally certified descendants of a federally recognized tribe located in Montana. Requires demonstrated financial need (at least $1 of remaining need) and about 12 months of Montana residency; covers tuition only, not fees. Renewable annually.

A $500 award for graduating high-school seniors (or GED completers), ages 17 to 21, in foster care, kinship care, adoptive, or resource families. Note the gate: the applicant's parent or another supportive adult must be a current NFPA member.

Three annual awards ($1,000 / $750 / $500) for college-bound students who were adopted or spent time in foster care and plan to attend a 4-year college. Selection weighs character, overcoming adversity, and academic progress. Due May 31.

rows.source_name: Montana Foster Youth Higher Education Assistance Program

fields.Name of Scholarship: Montana Foster Youth Higher Education Assistance Program
fields.Application Link/Method: Apply through your MUS campus financial aid office (foster youth / federal Chafee program)
fields.Summary: Last-dollar assistance for Montana foster youth eligible for the federal John H. Chafee program. Must enroll full-time in a degree, vocational, or entry-level professional credential program, have 12 months Montana residency, and have graduated high school or earned an equivalency. Apply through your MUS campus financial aid office.

An achievement- and leadership-based $20,000 award; 150 high-school seniors are selected each year. Open to all graduating seniors (not restricted by background) with a minimum 3.0 GPA. The application window runs August to September 30.

A $20,000 scholarship (plus laptop, textbook credits, and emergency aid) for Pell-eligible high-school seniors who participated in an approved college-readiness program in grades 11-12 and plan to enroll full-time at a four-year college. Rewards persistence over grades — minimum GPA is 2.4. Due February 15. Note the gate: you must have been in an approved college-readiness / college-access program.

For children of service members who died or became seriously injured in the line of duty since 9/11. Administered by Fisher House Foundation through the military scholarship portal (militaryscholar.org); a military-dependent / veteran-family award for graduating seniors entering an accredited college.

fields.Due Date: Annual — closes Mar 15 (apply after fall acceptance)
fields.Summary: For Montana high school seniors from Board of Public Education accredited schools pursuing a qualifying STEM or Healthcare major, enrolling full-time at an eligible Montana campus the fall after graduation. Requires 3.25 cumulative GPA plus 4 years college-prep math and 3 years college-prep science. STEM-focused, renewable annually if requirements are met.

rows.source_name: Montana FFA Foundation Leave a Legacy Scholarship

fields.Name of Scholarship: Montana FFA Foundation Leave a Legacy Scholarship
fields.Summary: Open to any Montana FFA member pursuing post-secondary education or trade/technical school. FFA membership is the gating criterion; a single unified application through the Reach Higher Montana portal qualifies applicants for all Montana FFA Foundation scholarships. Graduating high school FFA seniors are eligible.

fields.Due Date: Annual — closes noon (12 PM) Mon Apr 6, 2026
fields.Summary: Seven $1,000 scholarships for 2026 graduating high school seniors from Flathead, Lake, Missoula, or Ravalli Counties in Montana with a minimum 3.0 GPA, usable toward tuition, books, or expenses at any accredited college or trade school. Local/trades sponsor; apply by emailing the application plus a 500-word essay to Sherry@RhinoRoofingMt.com.

A $1,500 award administered by the Montana Farm Bureau Foundation to assist Montana Farm Bureau members and children of members pursuing higher education. Farm Bureau membership/family affiliation is the gating criterion; agriculture-oriented. Graduating high school seniors who are members or children of members are eligible.

rows.source_name: Montana Farm Bureau Women's Leadership Committee Scholarships

fields.Scholarship Location/Information: Montana Farm Bureau Federation — Women's Leadership Committee
fields.Name of Scholarship: Montana Farm Bureau Women's Leadership Committee Scholarships
fields.Summary: Two $1,500 scholarships from the MFB Women's Leadership Committee, available to both boys and girls graduating high school, who must be a current paid Montana Farm Bureau member or an immediate member of a current paid Montana Farm Bureau family. Agriculture/Farm Bureau affiliation is the gating criterion.

fields.Scholarship Location/Information: Montana FFA Foundation (endowed by Montana Agri-Business Assn. & Montana Grain Elevator Assn.)
fields.Summary: A $500 scholarship for Montana FFA members planning to study agriculture or the agricultural products industry (ag-business, grain industry, agri-business fields). Requires FFA membership and at least 2 years of agricultural education classes. Graduating high school FFA seniors in Montana are eligible; apply via the unified Reach Higher Montana / Montana FFA application.

One online application on the Kaleidoscope portal considers current FFA members for 120+ National FFA scholarships. Graduating high school seniors who are current FFA members qualify (under 23, planning to attend a US college, university, or trade school). Awards run up to $10,000 each.

fields.Due Date: Varies by local EAA chapter (chapters selected annually; no single national deadline)
fields.Scholarship Location/Information: National; administered through local EAA chapters (student must connect with a participating chapter)
fields.Summary: This aviation scholarship funds up to $12,000 toward a private/sport pilot certificate for youth ages 16-19 (15 for glider). Candidates are selected by a participating local EAA chapter, then screened by EAA — so a Whitefish senior must engage a chapter, complete a Young Eagles flight, and hold a student pilot certificate. High-school seniors in the age range qualify.
